what.zh: 陈平投汉、受金指控、六出奇计都在这一篇，篇幅不长，可以从“陳平既多以金縱反間”读起。
what.en: Chen Ping's defection, the bribery charge and his later stratagems are all in this short chapter.

what.zh: 从项羽一方看荥阳之围前后：请和、急围、范增离去、纪信诳楚。
what.en: The siege of Xingyang seen from Xiang Yu's side, including Fan Zeng's departure.

what.zh: 英文百科条目，概述陈平一生，适合入门；不是一手材料。
what.en: An overview of Chen Ping's whole career; a starting point, not a primary source.

what.zh: 韩信怎样从项羽帐下的郎中变成汉军大将，“印刓敝”那段评语也在这里。
what.en: How Han Xin went from a junior officer under Xiang Yu to Han's general, including his verdict on Xiang Yu.

episode.action: 项羽身边韩信陈平范增先后离开；反间计使范增求去

title.zh: 韩信、陈平、范增：项羽留不住的三个人
title.en: Han Xin, Chen Ping, Fan Zeng: The Three Men Xiang Yu Could Not Keep

dek.zh: 汉之三年，荥阳被围，汉王用四万斤金买一条离间计。同一场战争前后，项羽身边走了三个人——韩信、陈平、范增，走的理由各不相同，指向的却是同一件事。
dek.en: In the third year of the Han, with Xingyang under siege, the King of Han paid forty thousand catties of gold for a single stratagem of mistrust. Across that same war, three men left Xiang Yu's side — Han Xin, Chen Ping, and Fan Zeng — each for a different reason, and all three pointing at the same question: could Xiang Yu hold on to people?

heading.en: A Fine Banquet and a Crack

paras.zh: 汉之三年，项羽几番截断汉军甬道，荥阳城里的汉王断了粮，派人请和，条件是把荥阳以西割给汉。项羽本想答应，历阳侯范增拦住：「漢易與耳，今釋弗取，後必悔之。」——汉军眼下好打，放过了要后悔。楚军随即急围荥阳。
paras.en: In the third year of the Han, Xiang Yu cut the Han army's supply corridor again and again. Inside the walls of Xingyang the King of Han ran out of grain, grew afraid, and sued for peace, offering to cede everything west of the city to Han. Xiang Yu was ready to accept. Fan Zeng, Marquis of Liyang, held him back: "The Han is easy to deal with; let him go now without taking him, and you will regret it later." The Chu army promptly tightened its grip on Xingyang.

paras.zh: 照《史记》的写法，汉王这一次没有硬拼，而是让楚营自己生疑，出主意的是早先从项羽那边投来的陈平。项羽身边先后走了三个人：韩信在汉王入蜀时就走了，陈平随后投汉，最后是亚父范增求去。三人走的理由并不相同，合起来看，却都指向同一件事：项羽留不留得住人。
paras.en: By the Shiji's telling, the King of Han did not fight his way out this time. He got the Chu camp to sow suspicion on itself, and the idea came from Chen Ping, who had earlier come over from Xiang Yu's side. The episode opens onto a pattern: over these years three men walked away from Xiang Yu. Han Xin left first, when the King of Han went into Shu; Chen Ping followed, defecting to Han; and last came Yafu — "Second Father," the honorific by which Fan Zeng was known — asking to go. Their reasons differed, yet taken together they point at one thing: whether Xiang Yu could keep people at all.

paras.zh: 时间是汉之三年（一般折算为公元前204年），地点在荥阳，汉军被围、粮道被断。项羽身边有被尊为亚父的历阳侯范增，还有钟离眛、龙且、周殷等将领——按陈平的说法，这样的骨干「不過數人耳」。汉王那边，陈平此前已从楚营投来，任护军中尉，监护诸将；韩信更早一步，在汉王入蜀时便离开楚营。本文要讲的，就是这三个人各自的转身，以及最后一桌菜。
paras.en: The time is the third year of the Han (conventionally reckoned as 204 BC); the place is Xingyang, where the Han army was besieged and its supply road cut. Around Xiang Yu stood Fan Zeng, Marquis of Liyang, honored as Yafu, along with generals Zhongli Mo, Long Ju, Zhou Yin and others — hard-core supporters who, by Chen Ping's count, "were only a few." On the Han side, Chen Ping had already defected from Chu and held the post of Commandant Protector of the Army, supervising the generals; Han Xin had left Chu earlier still, at the King of Han's entry into Shu. What follows is the story of those three turnings, and of the last meal that closed the sequence.

paras.zh: 先走的是韩信。项梁渡淮时，他仗剑投奔，在项梁帐下没有什么名气；项梁败后，他转属项羽，项羽让他做郎中。他「數以策干項羽，羽不用」——多次拿计策去求见，项羽一概不用。到汉王入蜀那年，他离开楚营归汉。按原文，这比陈平投汉要早得多，那时荥阳之围还没有发生。
paras.en: Han Xin left first. When Xiang Liang crossed the Huai, Han Xin came along with a sword at his side and took service under him, and nothing was heard of him. After Xiang Liang's defeat he passed to Xiang Yu, who made him a gentleman-attendant at court. He "repeatedly pressed Xiang Yu with strategies, but Xiang Yu used none of them" — scheme after scheme went up, and none was adopted. In the year the King of Han went into Shu, Han Xin left Chu for Han. On the text's own timeline this was far earlier than Chen Ping's crossing; the siege of Xingyang had not yet happened.

paras.zh: 陈平的故事要从一口肉说起。乡里社祭，他主持分肉，分得非常均匀，父老夸「善，陳孺子之爲宰！」他回了一句大话：「使平得宰天下，亦如是肉矣！」——哪天让我宰天下，也这么分。陈胜起事后，他投奔魏王咎，魏王让他做太仆，他的说辞魏王不听，又有人进谗，他就走了；后来项羽略地到河上，他再去投，随项羽入关灭秦，赐爵卿。
paras.en: Chen Ping's story begins with a portion of meat. At the village sacrifice to the soil god he served as carver, and he divided the meat so evenly that the village elders called out: "Well done, young Master Chen — a fair carver!" He answered with a boast: "If I ever get to carve up the world, it will be just like this meat!" When Chen Sheng rose in rebellion, Chen Ping went to serve Wei Jiu, King of Wei, who made him Master of the Horses. His advice was not heeded, someone slandered him, and he left. Later Xiang Yu's forces campaigned as far as the river, and Chen Ping joined them, followed the army through the passes and the fall of Qin, and was rewarded with the noble rank of qing.

paras.zh: 真正让陈平离开楚营的，是一次功过倒挂。殷王反楚，项羽任陈平为信武君，带兵击降殷王而还，项王派项悍拜他为都尉，赐金二十溢。不久汉王攻下殷，项王大怒，「將誅定殷者將吏」——要杀当初平定殷地的那批人。陈平害怕了，把金和印都封好送还项王，自己带着剑抄小路逃走（原文作「間行杖劎亡」）。
paras.en: What actually drove Chen Ping out of Chu was merit repaid with danger. When the King of Yin rebelled against Chu, Xiang Yu made Chen Ping Lord Xinwu, gave him the former retainers of King Wei to command, and sent him to bring Yin to terms. He did, and returned in triumph; the King of Chu had Xiang Han appoint him Commandant and granted him twenty yi of gold. Not long afterward the King of Han took Yin. Xiang Yu flew into a rage and "was about to execute the officers who had settled Yin." Chen Ping, afraid for his life, sealed up the gold and his official seal, sent them back to the King of Chu by messenger, and slipped away by back roads with a sword at his side.

paras.zh: 逃亡路上还有一关。渡河时，船家见他一表人才、独自赶路，疑心是逃亡的将领，腰里揣着金玉，动了杀机。陈平干脆脱掉衣服，赤身帮着撑船——「解衣躶而佐刺船」——船家看清他身上什么也没有，才作罢。
paras.en: Even the flight had its hazards. Crossing a river, the boatman took in this fine-looking man travelling alone, guessed he was a runaway officer with gold and jewels in his sash, and thought of killing him. Chen Ping simply "stripped off his clothes and helped row the boat" naked. Seeing that he carried nothing, the boatman let the matter drop.

paras.zh: 到了汉营，麻烦换了形式。他经魏无知引见，当天就被拜为都尉、参乘、典护军，诸将一片哗然：一个楚军逃兵，凭什么监督军中老将。接着绛侯、灌婴等人告状，说他「盜其嫂」；在魏、在楚都待不住；如今管护军，还收将领的钱，「金多者得善處，金少者得惡處」，是个反覆乱臣。汉王召他责问，陈平答得直白：魏王不用他的计，他才去投项王；项王「不能信人，其所任愛，非諸項即妻之昆弟」，有奇士也用不上，他才离开。至于收钱，「臣躶身來，不受金無以爲資」——我光着身子来，不收钱就没有办事的用度。最后说：计策若无可采，钱都在，请封好交公，「得請骸骨」，放我走。汉王于是道歉、厚赐，拜他为护军中尉，尽护诸将，诸将不敢再说。
paras.en: In the Han camp the trouble merely changed shape. Introduced by Wei Wuzhi, he was received the same day and made Commandant, carriage companion to the king, and overseer of discipline in the army. The generals erupted: why should a fresh defector from Chu — one whose quality nobody knew — ride in the king's own carriage and supervise men older and senior to himself? Then the Marquis of Jiang, Guan Ying and others filed their accusations. He was "a fine-looking man, but like a cap ornament of jade — there may be nothing inside him." At home, they said, he had seduced his elder brother's wife. He had not been tolerated in Wei and had fled to Chu; he had not fit in there either and had fled again to Han. Now he held office, and he took the generals' money: "those who gave much got good postings, those who gave little got bad ones." A turncoat and a troublemaker — the king should look into him. The King of Han hauled Chen Ping over the coals, and Chen Ping answered flatly. King Wei had not used his plans, so he went to serve Xiang Yu; and Xiang Yu "could not trust people — those he relied on and favored were none but the Xiang clan and his wife's brothers," so even a rare talent had no chance there. As for the money: "I came with nothing but the clothes on my back; without taking gold I had nothing to work with." If any of his plans were worth using, use them; if not, the money was all there — seal it up and hand it over to the treasury, and "let me resign and go home." The king apologized, rewarded him richly, and appointed him Commandant Protector of the Army with full authority over the generals. The generals said no more.

paras.zh: 陈平看楚营，看到一条缝。项王身边的骨鲠之臣，亚父、钟离眛、龙且、周殷，「不過數人耳」；而项王「意忌信讒」，容易起疑。他请汉王拿出几万斤金行反间，离间楚军君臣。汉王给了黄金四万斤，「恣所爲，不問其出入」。钱撒进楚军，流言跟着起来：钟离眛等人为项王将兵，「功多矣，然而終不得裂地而王」，要与汉联手灭掉项氏、分地称王。项羽果然对钟离眛等人起了疑心。
paras.en: Studying the Chu camp, Chen Ping saw a crack. The men Xiang Yu truly relied on — Yafu, Zhongli Mo, Long Ju, Zhou Yin — "were only a few." And Xiang Yu "was suspicious by nature and quick to believe slander." Chen Ping asked the King of Han to put up tens of thousands of catties of gold for a campaign of deceit, driving a wedge between the Chu ruler and his ministers. The king handed over forty thousand catties of gold, "letting him do as he wished and never asking for an account." The money went out through the Chu army, and the rumors went with it: Zhongli Mo and the others had won much for the King of Chu as his generals, "yet never got a slice of territory to call their own," and wanted to join with Han, destroy the house of Xiang, and divide up its lands as kings. Xiang Yu did indeed begin to doubt Zhongli Mo and the rest.

paras.zh: 此时的亚父范增，与项羽相识已久，也早有分歧。范增是居鄛人，年七十，「素居家，好奇計」，当年劝项梁立楚怀王之后，说楚人至今怜念怀王，还引了「楚雖三戶，亡秦必楚」这句楚地的话。鸿门宴上，他「數目項王」，三次举起所佩玉珪示意，「項王默然不應」；宴后，亚父接过玉斗，放在地上，拔剑撞破，说：「唉！豎子不足與謀。」到分封诸侯时，是他与项王「陰謀」，拿巴蜀道险说事，把沛公封到巴蜀汉中。两人一起谋划过，也早有不合：鸿门宴上项王对他的示意默然不应，他事后骂出「豎子不足與謀」。
paras.en: Fan Zeng had known Xiang Yu for a long time by then, and the two had long had their differences. A native of Juchao, seventy years old, "a long-time stay-at-home who loved ingenious schemes," he had once come to advise Xiang Liang to restore the house of Chu: the people of Chu still grieved for King Huai, who had gone to Qin and never returned, and as the Chu saying ran, "Even if Chu has but three households left, the one to destroy Qin will surely be Chu." At the Feast at Hong Gate he "kept signaling the King of Chu with his eyes" and three times raised the jade tablet he wore at his belt as a signal; the king sat silent and did not respond. After the feast he took the jade dipper, set it on the ground, smashed it with his sword and said: "Bah! This boy is not worth plotting with. The man who takes the world from the King of Chu will surely be the Lord of Pei — we are all going to end up his captives." And when the fiefs were handed out, it was he and the King of Chu who "conspired," using the perilous roads into Ba and Shu as a pretext to pack the Lord of Pei off to Ba, Shu and Hanzhong. The two had planned together, and they had also already disagreed: at Hongmen Xiang Yu met his signals with silence, and afterwards Fan Zeng called him a "boy not worth planning with".

paras.zh: 离间计的最后一环，是一桌菜。项王派使者到汉营，汉王备下牛羊猪俱全的太牢，端上来，一见来人便装作吃惊：「吾以爲亞父使，乃項王使！」好菜撤下，换上粗劣的饭食。使者回去照实禀报，项王于是大疑亚父。范增主张急攻荥阳，项王不肯听；范增听说自己被疑，怒道：「天下事大定矣，君王自爲之！願請骸骨歸！」《项羽本纪》记项王许之。他还没走到彭城，背上发疽而死。
paras.en: The last link in the scheme was a meal. The King of Chu sent an envoy to the Han camp. The King of Han had a full taolao offering laid out — ox, sheep and pig — and carried in; then, catching sight of the visitor, he feigned astonishment: "I took this for Yafu's envoy — it is the King of Chu's envoy!" The fine dishes were carried away and coarse fare put before the man instead. The envoy went home and reported exactly what he had seen, and the King of Chu fell into deep suspicion of Yafu. Fan Zeng pressed for an immediate assault on Xingyang; Xiang Yu would not listen. Learning that he was suspected, Fan Zeng flared up: "The affairs of the world are settled, Your Majesty — see to them yourself! I ask to resign and take my old bones home!" The Basic Annals of Xiang Yu records that the king let him go. He had not reached Pengcheng when an ulcer broke out on his back, and he died.

paras.zh: 三个人离开，都绕着同一个字：予——给不给信任，给不给封赏。韩信后来对汉王评项王：勇，然「不能任屬賢將」，不过是「匹夫之勇」；待人「恭敬慈愛」，见人有病，涕泣分食饮，可到了有功该封爵的时候，「印刓敝，忍不能予」——大印在手里把棱角都磨圆了，也舍不得给出去，他称之为「婦人之仁」。陈平的分析几乎同调：项王「恭敬愛人」，所以「士之廉節好禮者多歸之」；「至於行功爵邑，重之」，舍不得封赏，于是「士亦以此不附」。一种解释是（作者推断）：反间计咬得住，正因为流言说的是「終不得裂地而王」，踩中了楚营里本就存在的不满。至于项羽为什么就这样信了，史书没有细讲。还要注意，韩信这番话和陈平这番分析都出自司马迁一人之笔，不能算两条独立证据。
paras.en: All three departures circle one word: giving. Do you give trust? Do you give reward? Han Xin later assessed the King of Chu for the King of Han. Brave, certainly — but he "could not entrust capable generals with responsibility," which made it "no more than a common man's courage." The courtesy was genuine: "when the King of Chu met people he was respectful and kind," weeping over a sick man's illness and sharing out his own food and drink. Yet when a man's merit called for a fief and a title, "the seal had its edges worn smooth, and he could not bear to give it up" — what Han Xin called "a woman's kindness." Chen Ping's analysis runs almost in parallel. Xiang Yu "was respectful and cared for men, and so men of integrity and good manners mostly rallied to him"; but "when it came to conferring fiefs and lands for merit, he weighed them grudgingly," and "men therefore did not attach themselves to him." One reading (the author's inference) is that the slander bit precisely because the rumor spoke of "never getting a slice of territory to call their own" — it landed on a grievance already alive in the Chu camp. Why Xiang Yu believed it so readily, the histories do not spell out. Note too that Han Xin's verdict and Chen Ping's analysis are both the work of Sima Qian's single pen; they are not two independent witnesses.

paras.zh: 还有一处值得留意（作者提出）：陈平和范增都说过骸骨。陈平说「得請骸骨」，是把去留交给汉王判断，结果被留下、被重用；范增说「願請骸骨歸」，是在被疑之后负气求去，项王也就放他走了。同样几个字，一次说在受质疑、去留还可商量的时候，结果被留下；一次说在信任破裂之后。至于太牢与粗食那一幕，情节太像戏，可能实有其事，也可能经过叙事加工，现有材料无法判断。
paras.en: There is another point worth pausing over (raised by the author). Chen Ping and Fan Zeng both asked for their bones — the old formula for resigning and going home. Chen Ping's "let me resign and go home" left the decision to the King of Han while his position was still open, and he was kept and promoted. Fan Zeng's "I ask to resign and take my old bones home" came after he had been suspected, spoken in pique, and the King of Chu simply let him walk. The same words, once while his place was still open to discussion, and once after trust had already broken. As for the scene with the fine dishes and the coarse fare — it plays like theater. It may have happened; it may have been shaped in the telling. The material we have cannot tell us which.

heading.en: What You Can Do With This Today

paras.zh: 一个小组里传出话：某位骨干拿了别家的邀约，快要走了。负责人的第一反应是去查谁在传话。更有用的第一个问题可能是：如果这话是真的，她为什么会想走？传言有人信，往往是因为它说中了一件大家心里都知道、却没人摆上桌面的事，比如一拖再拖的晋升。先处理那件事，传言就没那么有力了。
paras.en: Word goes around a small team: one of the core people has an offer from somewhere else and is about to leave. The lead's first instinct is to find out who is spreading the talk. The better first question may be: if the story is true, why would she want to go? Rumor sticks when it names something everyone already knows and nobody has put on the table — a promotion that keeps slipping, say. Deal with that, and the rumor loses much of its power.

paras.zh: 一个外包转正的同事接手采购，老同事私下嘀咕他会让熟人的供应商沾光。他没有赌咒发誓，只把三家比价的记录发进群里，每笔差价写明理由，谁都能翻。外来者要化掉怀疑，最省力的不是表态，是把过程摊开让人看。
paras.en: A colleague converted from contractor status takes over purchasing. Old hands mutter that he will tilt business toward suppliers he knows. He swears no oaths; he posts the three-way price comparison into the group chat, with the reason for every price difference spelled out where anyone can check it. For an outsider to dissolve suspicion, the cheapest move is not protest — it is laying the process out in the open.

paras.zh: 汉王把四万斤金交出去、连去向都不过问，放在今天是内控事故，不是气度；陈平用这笔钱买的是对手的猜疑，不是自己人的协作，别把离间当成管理术。这些材料实际上只有一条史源，太牢一幕尤其戏剧化。
paras.en: Handing forty thousand catties of gold to one man and never asking where it went would be an internal-controls failure today, not magnanimity. What Chen Ping bought with that money was the enemy's mistrust, not his own side's cooperation; do not mistake divide-and-rule for a management technique. And all of this rests on a single historical source, with the banquet scene especially theatrical.

paras.zh: 韩信「數以策干項羽，羽不用」是《史记》的记载，他评项王那番话出自他后来对汉王的说辞，同样出自司马迁转述；陈平陈述的离魏、离楚理由，是他面对汉王责问时的自述，可能带有自我辩护成分（作者推断）。范增被疑之后求去，是史书记下的结局；被疑之后留下来把话说清楚，或另起炉灶，都只是作者提出的可能，并不是史书记载的范增当时考虑过的选项。项羽、范增、韩信心里怎么想，原文没有写，本文也没有替他们想。
paras.en: That Han Xin "repeatedly pressed Xiang Yu with strategies, but Xiang Yu used none of them" is the Shiji's record; his verdict on the King of Chu comes from a speech of his own, delivered later to the King of Han, again relayed by Sima Qian. Chen Ping's stated reasons for leaving Wei and leaving Chu were his self-description under questioning by the king, and may carry self-justification (author's inference). That Fan Zeng asked to go after being suspected is the outcome the histories record; staying to clear the air, or starting over elsewhere, are possibilities the author raises, not options the histories show Fan Zeng weighing. What Xiang Yu, Fan Zeng and Han Xin thought to themselves is not in the sources, and this piece does not think it for them.

scenario.zh: 虚构：六个人的咖啡店后场团队，年底分红由店长一人定，方案照入职年限排。一位从别家跳槽来的烘豆师改进了拼配，出品口碑最好，却分得最少；店里已有传言，说店长只照顾老员工。
scenario.en: Fictional: a six-person back-of-house team at a coffee shop. The year-end bonus is set by the store manager alone, ranked by years of service. A roaster lured over from another shop improved the house blend and earns the best word of mouth for the drinks, yet gets the smallest share. Talk in the shop has it that the manager only looks after the old hands.

question.zh: 这位烘豆师应该留下来把分配规则谈清楚，还是另找一家店？留下意味着当那个挑刺的人，未必改得动，还可能被贴标签；离开干净利落，却等于默认这套规矩，也放弃了已经积累的手感和熟客。
question.en: Should the roaster stay and get the allocation rule out into the open, or look for another shop? Staying means being the one who picks at things — it may change nothing and earn him a label. Leaving is clean and quick, but it effectively concedes the rulebook and gives up the feel for the coffee and the regulars he has built up.

assumptions.zh: 假设他手里有硬数据（近两个月各人排班、出品与差评记录），店长并非恶意，只是惯性加怕麻烦；假设本地还有两三家店可以去。
assumptions.en: Assume he has hard data — two months of everyone's schedules, output and complaint records — and that the manager is not malicious, merely set in his ways and averse to trouble. Assume two or three other shops locally he could move to.

steps.zh: 先把排班与出品记录整理成一张表，只列事实；约店长单独谈一次，只谈规则口径，不谈人身；给出下次分红可采用的透明算法和一个过渡方案；若店长连列数据都不接受，再谈去留。
steps.en: First turn the schedules and output records into one table, facts only. Book a one-on-one with the manager and talk about the rule, never about personalities. Offer a transparent algorithm for the next bonus round plus a transitional arrangement. If the manager will not even look at the numbers, then discuss whether to stay or go.

alternative.zh: 另一种合理选择是直接走人，去一家分配有成文规则的店。理由是信任一旦塌了，重建的成本全由个人承担，而离开本身也是给店方和同行的信号。两种都合理，取决于他怎么判断这家店还有没有得改。
alternative.en: A reasonable alternative is simply to leave for a shop where written rules govern payouts. The argument: once trust has collapsed, the cost of rebuilding it falls entirely on the individual, and leaving is itself a signal to the shop and to the trade. Both choices are sound; it turns on how he judges whether this shop can still be changed.

uncertainty_note.zh: 全部材料出自司马迁《史记·陈丞相世家》《项羽本纪》《淮阴侯列传》以及班固《汉书》据《史记》的改写（A-E10 与 A-E4 同源），没有真正独立的第二史源；韩信评项王（A-E20）与陈平析项王（A-E2）虽可对照，但同出司马迁，不是互证。「太牢具—恶草具」一幕高度戏剧化，无从核对；「范增因反间而去」是《史记》给出的因果叙述（疑心→不听其计→求去→道中病死），不是独立证据；范增求去的原话两篇措辞不同（《陈丞相世家》作「願請骸骨歸」，《项羽本纪》作「願賜骸骨歸卒伍」）；陈平陈述的离魏、离楚理由出自他对汉王的自述，可能带有自我辩护成分（作者推断）；「盗嫂」「受诸将金」只是汉营诸将的指控，无独立核实；韩信「数以策干项羽」的具体内容原文未载；项羽、范增、韩信的内心活动原文未载，本文未写。本文只说韩信离开在「汉王之入蜀」时，早于陈平投汉，不另系具体年月。「汉之三年」折算为公元前204年依通行纪年，不出自本篇证据。
uncertainty_note.en: All materials come from Sima Qian's Shiji — the Hereditary House of Chancellor Chen, the Basic Annals of Xiang Yu, and the Memoir of the Marquis of Huaiyin — and from Ban Gu's Han Shu, which reworks the Shiji (A-E10 and A-E4 derive from the same account). There is no genuinely independent second source. Han Xin's verdict on the King of Chu (A-E20) and Chen Ping's analysis of him (A-E2) can be set side by side, but both come from Sima Qian and do not corroborate one another. The "fine dishes — coarse fare" scene is highly dramatic and cannot be verified. That "Fan Zeng left because of the stratagem of mistrust" is the causal narrative the Shiji gives (suspicion → his advice not followed → request to leave → death by illness on the road), not independent evidence. Fan Zeng's request to leave is worded differently in the two chapters (the Hereditary House of Chancellor Chen has "I ask to resign and take my old bones home"; the Basic Annals of Xiang Yu has "grant me my bones to return to the ranks"). Chen Ping's stated reasons for leaving Wei and leaving Chu are his own account to the King of Han and may carry self-justification (author's inference). "Seducing his elder brother's wife" and "taking the generals' money" are accusations made by generals in the Han camp, with no independent verification. The substance of Han Xin's "repeatedly pressed Xiang Yu with strategies" is not recorded. The inner thoughts of Xiang Yu, Fan Zeng and Han Xin are not recorded and are not written here. This piece says only that Han Xin left at "the King of Han's entry into Shu," earlier than Chen Ping's defection, and assigns no specific date to it. "The third year of the Han" is converted to 204 BC by the conventional chronology; that conversion does not come from the evidence in this piece.

length.basis: body + question + example; excludes sources and read-more
